So it is for you to deal with this. So I would like to draw your attention on this particular rule. Mr. Seselj, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, sir, I have no intention of invoking any sort of alibi. The indictment does not even allege that I was at the site of any of the crimes. Not only was I not a direct perpetrator, I wasn't even there when the crimes were committed. What I am being charged with primarily is hate speech, which I used to incite murderous instincts in others, rape instincts, looting instincts, and the desecration of places of worship. Then there is the joint criminal enterprise notion, which is a mere notion. There are no elements to it. According to that notion I should be responsible for any crime ever committed by the Serbs anywhere. That is the notional framework. As far as item B is concerned, under Rule 67, there is a partial specification, and then it says the things it says about mental accountability or responsibility of an accused. So that is a possible framework for a defence but this doesn't limit the individual variance of this special defence. I did understand that in good time and over the last years, I submitted to the OTP 15 documents in which I explained this special defence notion. The first report I submitted, which ran into over 300 pages, was an analysis of my political speeches where I spoke about how the Serbian soldiers and members of the Radical Serbian Party were to behave in war, how they were to treat the civilian population, children and so on and so forth. That was translated into English. The next report I wrote was a report in which I challenged the possibility of any sort of personal involvement on my part in a joint criminal enterprise. Even this concept that the OTP resorts to has no precedent in international criminal law. At the Nuremberg trials, there was the concept of conspiracy that was used but not joint criminal enterprise, which is what is being brought up here and which is what has been used already in a number of different trials here, which is a sore spot for this Tribunal generally speaking but that doesn't matter right now. Further, I wrote reports on the criminal role of the Roman Pope John-Paul II and Benedict XVI as the main culprits for the war in the former Yugoslavia. These reports run into over 4.000 pages, and contributions were made by Zoran Krasic and Elena Bozic-Talijan. This was even published in Belgrade in four volumes. The set contains four thick volumes. Further, I published three reports on what is here termed hate speech which runs into a lot of pages again, perhaps over 800, if you put it all together, citing examples of hate speech in Croatia by Croatian officials, by Croatian public figures, citing examples of hate speech by Muslim officials and figures of public life, and citing examples of hate speech by Western politicians, statesmen and leaders, speaking in very obvious terms about the Serbian people. And this was contributed to by Miro, a member of my expert team. And several other reports where I deal with the lack of reliability and moral credibility of certain OTP witnesses that were announced but who were not protected witnesses, or persons I assumed might appear as witnesses because they are on the OTP's bankroll and appear in other trials, (redacted), Dejan Anastasijevic, Vesna Kljajic and so forth -- and so on and so forth. So these persons are not protected witnesses which means I can use their names freely in open court. I disclosed that, but in one fell swoop, the OTP are trying to discredit this, as if I'd never done it to begin with. They have admitted themselves that they never read or translated some of those. Some of those they are not even familiar with. There is a motion to that effect by the OTP dated about two months ago. But I stick to those reports. These reports must be translated into English or French. Why? When my legal advisers examine me in this courtroom, in compliance with item B of Rule 67, they will be asking me about these reports. If you don't have it ready and in front of you in English or French, if you don't have it available, I don't know how on earth you're going to know what we are talking about. If you think that I'm going to try and prove that I'm totally unrelated to a rape that happened somewhere or other or to an act of mistreatment, that I first heard of after my arrival in The Hague, well, then, you are dead wrong. I will destroy this general historic framework that you so artificially built up in a series of trials before this Tribunal. But on account of their inadequate defence strategies, the accused so far have not been able to challenge that and to shatter this construct. I am thoroughly preparing just for that, and thank God you have provided me with ample time to prepare properly. Therefore, I'm not neglecting this rule. It was under this rule that I filed 15 reports which I'm not giving up regardless of the qualifications heaped on them by the OTP. These reports cannot be ignored because the entire strategy of my defence will be based on these reports and studies. I am being charged with all these things but for these things I will be using their own Popes, John-Paul the II and Benedict the XVI and I'm going to be accusing them of these crimes. I cannot be a worst criminal than Alija Izetbegovic, Franjo Tudjman, Bill Clinton, Madeleine Albright, Jacques Chirac or Tony Blair and I will be proving this in this courtroom and I will prove it well and soundly. I don't know who can stand in my way and who can keep me from doing that. I'm not going to be wasting my energy analysing if someone cursed someone else's Muslim mother, if someone killed somebody else for profit. I'm not going to be trying to convince anyone that it wasn't my fault that a murderous instinct awoke in a particular person, that somebody instinctively felt the need to loot or to kill people around him. I'm not going to be challenging these because this is something that the OTP simply cannot prove.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... A, B, by sending a 15 documents to the Prosecution. But as you know, the document which you have forwarded, do these documents also contain lists of witnesses which you intended to call to testify to prove your point? Otherwise, the Prosecution can turn around and say, "I have received the documents, but these documents do not contain the names of the witnesses."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, sir, I do not need to have any witnesses. Rule 67, item -- paragraph 1, item (B) says the names and addresses of witnesses and any other evidence. I will not be bringing any witnesses because that would be an irrational thing to do. In part, however, the defence experts will be addressing the issue in their expert reports. I limited myself to this particular portion, any other evidence. In my studies, I invoke with great precision a number of books, newspaper pieces, when I say books this means works of research, works of scholarship, historical scholarship. I also invoke documents produced by the Serbian secret services, especially as concerns certain witnesses on the OTP's payroll who are being overpaid, (redacted) (redacted). I invoke all of those and each of my studies and reports contains the appropriate references.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Line 24 of page 51, the names have not come up here. I hope, sir, that there are no protected witnesses that you are referring to. I do not know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly not. I'm keeping that in mind 100 per cent. I will not be disclosing a single protected witness name, at least not before protection measures are lifted. However, I will be applying great effort towards that objective, for protective measures to be lifted, and for the total number of protected witnesses to be reduced to what can be considered --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... To Rule 67 you have just told me that you have told the Prosecutor of your special mean of defence and it's now for the Prosecutor to see what's in there. And I expect that to happen very soon. Now, since last time, I have ruled on a number of issues and I would like to give you an indication of these because you may not have received the translation. Ms. Dahl, you wanted to respond on the Article 67 issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour we would like an opportunity before the transcript is released to review it for redaction because I share the Court's concern that perhaps there were materials mentioned that shouldn't have been. I'd like to clarify that on 22 November 2006, the previous Chamber issued an oral ruling at transcript page 812 to 813 that the material mentioned by Mr. Seselj today, which is the same as being discussed previously, was not within Rule 67, and I would note that on November 8 and November 3, there was quite a bit of discussion of the types of material Mr. Seselj considered to be a special defence. It was clarified at that point by Mr. Seselj that it was not within the express meaning of Rule 67 but that he considered it special because it was unique or presented for the first time and we considered that all of the issues were fully discussed and that there would be no reason to revisit the decision of the 22nd of November.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am bound only by what I say and what I rule. It says here in Article 67 that the accused may refer to a defence of alibi or a special defence. I have therefore turned to the accused and asked him to tell us whether he wants to act on the basis of Rule 67. He has just told me that on the issue of the defence of alibi he does not intend to act upon it and as for the special defence, he has just said that he has done what it takes and he has given me an explanation. I therefore do not feel I'm in a position to say whether what he is saying comes under the remit of Rule 67 or doesn't. What I do know is that Article 67 -- that Rule 67 entitles him to act, vis-a-vis the Prosecution and he feels what he has transmitted and handed over to you comes under special defence. Me, personally, as the Chamber I have nothing to say. First of all, because I have not seen these documents, I do not know what they include, Mr. Seselj has given us a quick summary of them, and he has also stated that he intends to refer to these documents during cross-examination and the examination of expert witnesses. So it's a question for you and him to settle. I have nothing to do in this. My only rule is to remind the accused that he has a number of rights, including this specific right under Rule 67, you may interpret this differently. He interprets it in his own way. But once again, it is not for me to say that his interpretation of Rule 67 is erroneous. It's his business, it's not mine. Maybe we misunderstood each other, Ms. Dahl.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: I'm in agreement with the Chamber. I was pointing out that this was not new ground to be ploughed. That it had been addressed previously for the Court's information and whether it withstands the requirements of rules and whether he has complied with what's incumbent upon him under the rules remains to be seen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Mr. Seselj, you wanted to answer back to Ms. Dahl, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, I think that it was precisely in this courtroom that I testified for 14 days as a defence witness in the Milosevic case. As for three of these reports, I presented my opinions on that during my testimony there, and even the Prosecutor prepared his questions for cross-examination on the basis of these reports, as regards these particular individuals. May I draw your attention to another thing? This manner that Prosecution counsel has, it seems to her that there may be something here that should not be disclosed but she doesn't know what it is, so she's going to look at it and speak on the subject subsequently. I mentioned three witnesses, I testified about them in the Milosevic case. (redacted), I testified in public

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: (redacted).But as a name, as an individual, he's not a protected witness. People know, the public knows, that he testified here in several trials and I spoke about him here on the basis of three concepts of my special defence, and that is what I did as a defence witness in the Milosevic case. Please do not allow such insinuations that somebody says, "It seems to me that there may be something there." You either know or you don't know that there is something there. I was very accurate, and I pay special attention to this, and so far I've made no mistakes on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, my concern was to act in accordance with the protocol that was established for reviewing the transcripts in an abundance of caution. There were no insinuations of misconduct being made presently against Mr. Seselj. What we would like to do is simply review it before it goes out. I'm rather new to the case and want to avoid unnecessary inadvertent mistakes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, registrar, I suppose we should check indeed that the witnesses that have been mentioned are not protected witnesses. I do not know. I understand that there is a -- somebody called (redacted) [as interpreted]. I have no idea who he is. According to Mr. Seselj, his testimony did not happen while he was a protected witness so that's all I know. Let us now move on to the next item, rulings recently given. The Trial Chamber -- the Chamber or myself, rather, have ruled on the Cermak and Markac issue relating to the access of confidential documents in the Seselj case. This was rejected -- thrown out in the ruling. On the 29th of May, I gave a ruling on the protection of witnesses. That's what I mentioned earlier, and I said how we should proceed. I also ruled on the preliminary memo and the list of evidence under 65 ter on the 31st of May, and I have asked Prosecution to hand this over swiftly. Mr. Seselj, there was also a very important ruling that was made. You may have received a copy of it if it has been translated and I don't know that it has yet. This ruling relates to the motion by the accused to set a deadline to file a pre-judgement motion, a preliminary judgement, on the summary indictment -- the summary modified indictment, motion number 287. The Chamber, under the chairmanship of Presiding Judge Robinson, has accepted this motion, and therefore entitles the accused to file a preliminary motion based on an error in the form of the amended summary indictment. Therefore, a 14-day period will run as of the translation of the motion or of the 14 motions under motion 285. Mr. Seselj, I remember that you said last time that you wanted to challenge the indictment. Our ruling enables you to do so. The deadline runs from the moment when you will have received this ruling translated into your own language. This is something that I wish to inform you of. There is also another motion that was slightly confidential and I will therefore ask the registrar to put us back into private session. And I will give the floor to the Prosecution afterwards because I want to wrap up on this final point first. Registrar, please, closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Dahl, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: I wanted to indicate that the intersection between those two rulings presents a conundrum for the timetable under which Mr. Seselj is to file his challenge to the indictment. Under the Chamber's ruling, the last triggering date is service of one of the -- of the Rule 66(A)(i) statements. We are in the process of disclosing those materials presently. However, the delayed disclosure of some -- a subset of those statements allows us to wait until 30 days before trial. That would delay the timetable under the Chamber's order to challenge the indictment, and I would like to request modification of that decision. I can put the request in writing, if that will be more helpful, so that the non-protected witness statements, the service of those, will then be the triggering event and that we are not put -- the case is not put in the position of having the challenge to the indictment coming on the opening of the trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. I will look into this. The issue of course is not wasting -- of not wasting any time, and to do so we have to make sure that Mr. Seselj can have the possibility very soon of filing his motions on the indictment, and that he also has access to these 14 statements should they serve any purpose in his defence. In the ruling that Judge Robinson has signed and which I can read here, it states that the 30-day period runs from the moment when Mr. Seselj gets the translation in B/C/S, and it also indicates that it may run from the moment when he receives the documents under Rule 66(A)(i). Now, because we now have this order I think we should act upon it very swiftly so that we shouldn't waste any time. Afterwards, the Trial Chamber, as a whole, will have to look at it, seeing as it is a preliminary motion. I have not -- I cannot act on the authority of the Trial Chamber as a whole, so the Trial Chamber as a whole will have to rule on this preliminary motion on the basis of the questions raised by Mr. Seselj, should there be any. And this may also take some time. Let me also mention -- let me also mention the issue of motion 288. There were also a number of issues related to confidentiality and I would therefore ask the usher to -- the registrar, sorry, to go into closed [sic] session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are now in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. So we are back in public session, then -- open session. I heard that the wall was being broken down. I don't know where we've got to. Maybe the construction work is finished. Can you tell me more, maybe?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I was told that work on this would start on Friday. By this morning, work hadn't started yet. But it wouldn't surprise me if work was already underway now and had started after I left the cell. I certainly received every possible guarantee that the matter would be dealt with swiftly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the course of a Status Conference, I remember giving the undertaking, and I will stick to it, that I would come and see by myself that indeed you do enjoy the best possible facilities so as to enable you to work from your cell. I was therefore waiting until the end of this demolition work before I would come and visit you. Now, we will come back on the 4th of July and you will tell me on the 4th of July when it is agreeable to you for me to come and visit you, together with the registrar, of course, to witness by my own eyes that it has been done. I'll just remind you that as of the 12th of July, I shall not be in The Hague so I will come between the 4th and the 12th, provided the demolition work is done. Just goes to show that it made sense for me to raise this issue because I had been told, or at least I was under the impression that the demolition work had started and you're telling me that it hasn't. I therefore sincerely hope that it will start very shortly so we will discuss this issue once again on the 4th of July and I hope that we will have finished the demolition work by then and that you will have a free access to the second cell so that you can have easy access to all your documents. I'd also like to -- are there any other comments on this issue, Mr. Seselj?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I do have another question to raise, if I may. Yesterday I filed a motion for the Trial Chamber to reconsider its ruling on the 15th of May. This is the contempt of court proceedings, the request for contempt of court proceedings, for this to be delayed until the end of trial which is the suggestion that you made yourself. For reasons that I can't understand, this was served on me eight days too late. However, there is another argument that I would like to raise, which I came across as I received your ruling. The ruling was made on the 15th of May and I received it on the 1st of June. Therefore I had no time to draw the attention of my legal advisers to the documents so that they may incorporate it into the motion. In footnote 2 to that order, it reads that the OTP had submitted a reply to the contempt of court proceedings. There are ten confidential attachments and an ex parte attachment. I didn't get the reply at all. This was filed by the OTP on the 12th of April and has not been translated into Serbian or served on me, for example. Judge, sir, you know that under Rule 126 bis, I'm entitled to seek explanation from the Chamber for the submission of a reply to any motion made by the OTP. The time for filing responses to motions. I've not been able to do that so far because I still don't have the OTP motion. It hasn't been served on me and it would seem to follow from that same thing that the Trial Chamber could not make an order based on my motion based solely on the motion and reply by the OTP without allowing me to formally file a response. This is just another -- another argument in favour of you altering the 15th of May order. The urgency of a contempt proceedings is paramount here. Your order speaks to the fact that there is a suspicion, suspicion of contempt having been committed. Had there not been this suspicion you would have thrown my motion out any way. Any delay in these proceedings would be an obstruction of justice. This is a very important preliminary matter that must be dealt with before the trial begins. So, having raised this additional point, I think I have now shown sufficiently that the order must be reconsidered and amended. The order itself violates one of my basic procedural rights under Rule 126 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if I understand you rightly, Mr. Seselj, and I must say, I had overlooked this, you have not had the answer of the Prosecution; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not to this very day. The response is dated the 12th of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. Under Rule 126 bis, when a party answers, they can be the possibility for the other party to be allowed to answer back by the Chamber. This, of course, would require you to have been given the preliminary answer. I now understand you haven't received it. Well, I will look at my colleague -- I will turn to my colleagues and this was a Trial Chamber's ruling as a whole, and I therefore must consult them. I personally would be ready to give you more time to answer back but I am not sure I know what my colleagues would say. I will therefore consult them and you're quite right to have drawn my attention to this issue. I expect my colleagues had not taken into account or realised the issue of the translation. What I expect is that the Prosecution's answer went to translation and translation -- that translation of the document didn't occur or was happening and therefore you didn't get it in time and has not -- you have not been in a position to answer back. So thank you for telling me and I will consult and tell my colleagues immediately, enabling you to act upon this. Let me now turn to Ms. Dahl. We have noticed, Madam, that there are a number of outstanding issues that are still pending, the issue of funding by the Tribunal of his associates, the 207.000 pages, the issue also of the indictment that will be called into question by the accused, and all sorts of other things. I think we all now know what these issues are. Now, over and beyond these current problems, I think we should look to the future. And when I say we should look to the future, I think we should establish a working mechanism that Prosecution -- or working plan that the Prosecution could submit to the Chamber, bearing in mind the possibility of new modifications and amendments on the indictment. What I'm more interested in is working on the basis of the 65 ter list and understand how you will get the witnesses to come, the viva voce witnesses, the 65 ter witnesses, and the others. What is your working plan, what do you expect to do? I will also have to tell you and to decide on how much time you will have for the presentation of the evidence on the basis of all these elements. I know that the trial started and was then suspended because of the counsel issue. I seem to remember that you had provided for six months for the presentation of evidence, give or take a little time. Six months is so many hours. So on the basis of your working plan, I will have to look, witness by witness, how much time we should expect to spend with them. I therefore need to know what you intend to do and I need to get a sense and an understanding of how you are going to present the evidence, and that means, of course, that I need to know who are going to be your witnesses, how -- who comes and testifies viva voce, who is going to be 92 bis, 92 ter. I need all this so that I can prepare the work of the Chamber and also so that the accused, who will be organising his own defence, can organise it precisely because he needs to know who the witnesses are and who they will be coming and how -- in which order they will be coming. He needs to be informed upstream. So I just wanted to mention this. And I'm sure that we will have opportunities to come back to this issue, and I wanted to highlight the fact that this is a significant concern that I have and that presumably the accused shares. So that he can organise his defence depending on who comes and which witnesses come. After all, cross-examination also has to be properly prepared. During the next Status Conferences, we will have an opportunity, I am sure, to discuss with Mr. Seselj and yourself all the issues that arise. Now, before I sum up the Status Conference, after all, I am working on another case this afternoon, I would like to turn to Mr. Seselj one final time and ask him whether there are any other items that he wishes to raise today for the information of the Trial Chamber or the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Judge, sir. I have raised all my points for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, I must also ask you the usual questions on your health. Are you in good health?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I'm all right. No problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. And as far as your conditions of detention are concerned, are there any particular requests or grievances you would like to make or are you waiting for the work to be completed in this famous cell?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no grievances for the time being. I have received every assurance that this would be finished in a matter of days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Ms. Dahl, would you like to draw my attention or the attention of the Trial Chamber on any particular point?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: The overwhelming majority of motions that are pending before the Chamber have to do with planning for the trial and what method we will be presenting testimony. I will endeavour to present two pictures to the Chamber regarding the duration of the case. One is if we are in need of bringing more witnesses than planned in viva voce format, and whether the amount of time that is represented by using the procedures under the rules, it's my understanding that Mr. Seselj has a strong objection to so-called paper testimony, and we will look at our case to see how best to present it. We want to achieve a coherent and cogent narrative for the finders of fact and that perhaps is best served by favouring the viva voce witnesses but we will certainly streamline and present the most persuasive concise case possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Seselj, I would just like to put a question to you. This is something which I have noticed in the written submissions. This has to do with the 92 ter witnesses. In your written submissions, you are against the fact that these witnesses fall under the 92 ter rules provisions. Let me reassure you, the 92 ter rule does entitle to you cross-examine these witnesses. 92 ter rule is a fairly simple rule; we have a written statement in this case. The witness has prepared this written statement. The witness has signed it. And he is then being asked a while ago, in 2002, 2003, 2004, I don't know, "You made this statement. Is this your statement?" And he says, "Yes." "Is this your signature?" And he says, "Yes." "Would you like to amend something today?" Sometimes in certain cases some witnesses say yes. Because they remembered a number of facts or they remembered that what they have stated is not quite in line with what they said at the time. So then changes are made. And after that, the Prosecutor says, and this is a very swift process, "I would like to tender into evidence the written statement." The accused then has the floor and the accused cross-examines the witness on the entirety of the document. But in this -- at this particular stage, the documents are being authenticated by the witness. Certain documents are shown by the Prosecution to the witness and the witness is asked to comment upon them. And as part of the cross-examination, the accused then cross-examines the witness and says, in paragraph 1, you have said such and such, and you cross-examine the witness. I wanted to make sure that you had no doubts about this. The Prosecutor is not tendering into evidence a document which nobody is allowed to talk about. The Prosecution -- the accused plays a great part because the accused cross-examines the witness, and the judges on the Bench also put questions to the witness, put questions about the documents, about what the witness has written and so on and so forth. This is a fairly new procedure, which is advantageous because we are able to gain time in this case. And very often, the -- during the Prosecution case, the witness answers questions which are put by the Prosecution. So in certain instances we are able to gain time and the Prosecution is still -- and the accused can cross-examine this witness. As this witness figures on the 65 ter witness list, and the time allocated to the Prosecution is mentioned on this document, an hour and a half, for instance, the Defence will automatically have the same time, i.e. an hour and a half, even if the Prosecution spends ten minutes with this witness, the accused will have an hour and a half to cross-examine that witness. I wanted to share this with you because in your written submissions, I understand that you were worried about it. Mr. Seselj, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed, Judge, sir, there are two problems inherent in this. One has surfaced repeatedly already. I really am adamant that the number of 92 bis testimonies, 92 ter and 92 quater, be reduced to a minimum. The bulk of evidence must be viva voce. In principle, the evidence under the three said rules should not amount to more than 10 per cent of the total evidence. Secondly, before you and your colleagues agree to have a certain statement made by a witness admitted under 92 bis, 92 ter and 92 quater, the OTP must submit to both you and me the material in its totality: Any statements made by these witnesses, any evidence they gave in other trials, and any possible accompanying documents. They must do this before I am bound to state my position whether it is acceptable for me for any of these witnesses to be introduced under any of these rules. The OTP are doing it exactly the other way around. They want you to grant these witnesses being introduced under these rules ahead of time, as it were. And then in God knows how many months, I will be caught up in a situation where I will have to acquaint myself quickly with the essence of their evidence, the gist of their evidence. I must know what the essence of their evidence is under these rules and then I can make my move. It isn't enough for me to know that a witness has died and then his statement is submitted under 92 bis. Maybe it's sufficient for that witness. If he's dead, he cannot be here. But it's certainly not sufficient for me to allow his statement to be introduced under a certain rule. It must be better argumented, as it were. The trial is four and a half years late. Half my witnesses will die before the trial ever begins. People are fragile beings. They are gone in a minute, especially all these false witnesses, suddenly their conscience awakes, they have compunction and they commit suicide, or something simply eats them up from inside. These are dangerous matters, you know, and they are certainly not a game. There must be a study in relation to each and every witness planned to be submitted under Rule 92 bis, ter or quater. We must list everything that puts me in connection with this witness and then I can say, "This one okay, 92 bis, this one okay, 92 ter, this one okay, 92 quater." But if I say that I can't accept one of these witnesses under any of these rules, I must know exactly why and I must have appropriate reasons. Things being what they are, I can state, ahead of time and as a matter of principle, I don't agree. And then you say but you don't furnish any argument, do you? How could I possibly furnish any argument if I've never received any documents whatsoever?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Insofar as some witnesses can come in different forms, 92 ter, 92 bis and 92 quater, viva voce, viva voce and 92 ter witnesses can be cross-examined by you. As far as 92 bis witnesses are concerned, as you know, these are witnesses which meet very precise criteria and under Rule 92 bis, the criteria should be mentioned in the Prosecution's motion and should be clearly spelled out, to see whether there is any need to hear these witnesses, and under Rule 92 bis, it is stated that these testimony must be cumulative as compared with other witnesses, therefore the Prosecution should explain why this testimony is cumulative in nature, should pertain to the historical political or military background in question, and statistical analysis of ethnic -- of ethnicity, has to relate to the crimes committed on victims, on the character of the accused, or has to do with information that has to be considered when handing down the sentence. And some factors are quite the opposite, that the evidence be presented orally, that a party may object because it feels that this is not reliable, and any other factor that would substantiate a cross-examination. So this procedure is subject to a number of criteria and it will be for the Chamber to hand down a judgement. I cannot take a decision at this juncture on these 92 bis witnesses. Last time, I explained that it has -- it is shaped like a triangle. We have viva voce witnesses, 92 ter witnesses, who come to corroborate what viva voce witnesses have said, and then we have 92 bis witnesses that corroborate all of this, but basically the whole system rests on the testimony of viva voce witnesses. This is what I said last time. When a viva voce witness has just discussed a number of events or facts, a 92 ter witness will address the same events but maybe it is not necessary to examine him on all the events in question. So this is how Rule 92 ter is being applied. You raised the 92 ter -- 92 quater issue. We do face a situation, some of the witnesses have died unfortunately, and these witnesses have made written statements or these witnesses have testified, either under oath or have testified during the Prosecution case and have been cross-examined. In certain cases, this evidence provided by these witnesses may be of interest in the particular case, maybe of interest to the Prosecution or may be of interest to the Defence. You may want to tender into evidence the testimony of a witness who has died because you feel that this is particularly important, and this procedure enables to you do this. So this is how the system works. I know that 92 quater is something which you've referred to. You are thinking of Mr. Babic, and you are referring to what has been said in the Milosevic trial. Unless I'm mistaken, I believe that that is what you are referring to. Maybe you're referring to other things as well. I don't know. But we will know which will be the viva voce, 92 ter, 92 bis and 92 quater witnesses. We will be hearing as soon as the witness list is drawn up. And it's only when that is done that we will be able to see where we stand.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The OTP provided a general list of witnesses. In my opinion, it was done before the indictment was reduced, because I indicated to you last time that there are many crime based witnesses on that list, from Vocin, Brcko, Bijeljina, Samac, et cetera and all of that is no longer in the indictment. So again, the OTP has not done its work conscientiously and properly. First they should submit a list of viva voce witnesses, and that is something that they undeniably have the right to do. For everything else, the OTP have to be granted leave by the Trial Chamber and before you rule on this, I have to have time to challenge it because, say, even in 92 bis you can have a character witness. There are at least a million people who are prepared to write the worst of things about my character and then I don't have the opportunity to cross-examine them and to prove that their character is far worse, and in this way make them totally incredible and therefore their statements would not even be taken into consideration. Then in accordance with 92 ter, there is this trend in the OTP, in other cases, to call as many witnesses as possible under 92 ter under the exclusive argument of saving time in this way. However, under Rule 92 ter, every witness can charge me in the same way in which viva voce witnesses can charge me, whereas my time for cross-examination is limited. In the Milosevic case, it was from 45 minutes to an hour and a half. And then for example, 200 documents are tendered along with such a witness. He cannot -- this kind of witness cannot even mention all the documents involved. And so on and so forth. Last time, I gave the example of the insider witness who was supposed to be their crown witness, in December last year, this -- and now they have submitted a request to turn that witness VS-17 it into a 92 ter witness. All of a sudden, this star witnesses changes his status. It just crossed their mind. Do you know why? Because the OTP writes that person's statement and then they are afraid that that witness will not be able to tell that story as nicely as they wrote it in his statement, because this is not his own statement, it's somebody else's. It's the OTP that created the statement. Then I'm going to be constrained in terms of my cross-examination time and anything goes. As for 92 quater, an according to my calculation, there are six witnesses that died, Milan Babic; Miroslav Deronjic; then a Muslim officer from Mostar; then an alleged volunteer from Novi Sad; another one committed suicide, the OTP asked for protective measures to be lifted but I haven't got the decision yet as to whether these measures were lifted or not. I'm going to mention any names although they know who this is. And one person was killed because he took part in Arkan's assassination. He was killed on some vendetta. So, along with Milan Babic, I already gave you this example, they want to tender about 300 documents. I have forgotten the exact number but I told you because I had the exact survey, through a dead witness they want to tender 300 documents. I don't think that a single document of a general nature can be introduced through a dead witness because the point of introducing documents through witnesses is that I should have an opportunity to ask that witness specific questions about a given document, not saying automatically, let's introduce 300 documents, or for example in the case of 92 ter, I get an hour or an hour and a half for cross-examination and several hundred documents accompany that witness's statement. I should be given the opportunity to put at least one question respectively with regard to each and every one of these documents. Let the OTP reduce the number of documents or let them count on a lot more time. I cannot use less than three minutes for putting questions for each and every document. If you have several thousand documents, then multiply that by five minutes, for instance and you're going to see how much time that is for cross-examination on documents only. And then, clarify this for yourselves: How many irrelevant documents there are there. Because I have the right to put questions with regard to relevancy, not just to give me a bit of time to ask him what's his name, what kind of schools he went to and so on. You know, the main point of cross-examination is to challenge the credibility of a witness. I am going to ask him about his mother's milk, that he was fed when he was a baby and I'm going to prove even through that that he cannot be a credible witness. I repeat my insistence yet again, as for 92 bis, ter and quater, I should have a minimal number of witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What you are saying has been recorded. We will be able to see things much more clearly once we have a new list, but just one remark I'd like to make. Given that the indictment has been amended, the Prosecution withdrew 26 witnesses from its original witness list, but before we can do anything we need to have the definitive witness list. As now the time has come to adjourn, I'd like to thank you and we shall meet again on the 4th of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
